correctness.rationale: The unimodular-index-2 coordinate change turns the intrinsic diamond into a square and torus fibers into circles of length two. For r<1/2 each ball intersects a generic fiber in at most one interval of length 2r and is active on a v-set of measure 2r. Integrating the integer lower bound on active intervals proves the exact slice inequality. A lattice of diamond centers tiles at r=1/(2n), and the area bound matches its 2n² centers. The plateau follows. Exact-rational checker passed 1,456 sampled torus points, but proof is independent of sampling.

value.rationale: The missed three-cover phase is a natural exact small-k threshold on a compact geometric product, not an arbitrary slice. Its obstruction is stronger than elementary area in an open radius range and admits infinite sharp resonant instances. It is directly motivated by low-dimensional gaps in a new general sum-product covering conjecture and may serve as a test invariant for other normed quotient geometries.
